text:
Ari Gomez: quick follow-up from the runtime section in today's all-hands — posting the decisions we made and open questions. please drop short Qs and I'll triage. :point_down:
Mike Chen: Thanks Ari. For the batching notes, can you confirm the new target for tail latency at p95 with 4k context on T4-class instances?
Ari Gomez: target p95 = 120ms for typical 4k generation workloads (single-request path). that's with continuous batching and prefix cache enabled.
Sara Patel: Is that with the new kernel priority scheduling enabled? curious about degraded cases when we hit high concurrency.
Ari Gomez: yes — kernel priority scheduling + short batching window (max_delay_ms=5) by default. degrade path: if GPU utilization > 85% we route to a cost-tier fallback model variant.
Leah Ortiz: how are we measuring the 120ms? synthetic vs production traces? we need to ensure evals match real request distributions.
Ari Gomez: measured from production-like replay (our eval harness) taking client-size distributions. we'll publish the harness config. action: publish replay config and seed prompts.
Mike Chen: follow-up: can we get the exact autoscale thresholds? last canary had a regression because scale-up lagged.
Ari Gomez: autoscale policy: scale-out when GPU queued_tokens > 50k for 30s; scale-in when queued_tokens < 10k for 60s. tuning note: we're experimenting with an anticipatory scaler that uses short-term request-rate derivative.
Zane Cole: to add, ops will run a stress canary that exercises corner-case KV cache misses. we saw a cache cold-start causing double inference spikes.
Sara Patel: +1 on the cache cold-start. any plan for warming prefix cache during rollout?
Ari Gomez: plan: staggered rollout where early canaries run a warmup job that replays hot prefixes. also we have a fallback: short-term LRU cache persisted to local SSD for fast restart.
Mike Chen: can you share the warmup job snippet?
Ari Gomez: sure — example below:
```
# warmup job (k8s job snippet)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: runtime-warmup
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: warmup
        image: registry/redwood/runtime-warmup:stable
        args: ["--replay-file", "/data/hot-prefixes.json", "--parallelism", "8"]
```
Leah Ortiz: about kernels: any progress on the new fused attention kernel for long contexts? is that going to be gated behind a runtime flag?
Ari Gomez: fused attention v2 is landing in the next canary. initially behind feature flag `fused_attn_v2=true` to let us compare. rollback plan exists if memory growth observed.
Sara Patel: sizing question — does fused_attn_v2 increase memory usage per layer? we need to update Dedicated sizing docs.
Ari Gomez: small increase ~6% in peak activation memory at 8k context for some models. we'll add explicit numbers to the sizing docs. action: update sizing doc and notify sales/solutions.
Mike Chen: one more — quantized kernels: any ETA for per-layer dynamic quantization support? some customers prefer int8 to cut cost.
Ari Gomez: roadmap: experimental per-layer int8 in Q3, GA after perf regressions are addressed. threading with CUDA kernels is the main blocker.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for fused_attn_v2 on 6 nodes in us-west-2 at 11:07am UTC.
Mike Chen: noted. will monitor canary dashboards.
Leah Ortiz: can we get a small checklist for SRE on what to watch during the canary?
Ari Gomez: yes — short checklist: 1) increase in p99 latency > 15% 2) GPU mem OOMs 3) queued_tokens spike 4) error-rate > 0.5% 5) KV cache miss-rate > baseline+10%. I'll DM ops to pin to the canary runbook.
Sara Patel: thanks. can we also log kernel versions in traces so we can correlate regressions quickly?
Zane Cole: good call — adding kernel_version tag to span when present. will include in next tracing deploy.
Mike Chen: any follow-up meetings planned? a quick triage sync would help.
Ari Gomez: scheduling a 30-min runtime triage tomorrow 16:00 PT. agenda: canary status, warmup effectiveness, autoscale tuning. 15-min pre-reads will be posted.
Leah Ortiz: I'll prep a short slide on evaluation distributions and edge cases.
Mike Chen: I'll bring recent canary dashboards and the scale event logs.
Sara Patel: I'll update the sizing doc PR and link it in the pre-reads.
Ari Gomez: great — thanks everyone. if you have small questions drop them here; for longer items ping me or create an issue in runtime/triage. :thumbsup:
